newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani president leaves for Uzbekistan.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani president leaves for Uzbekistan.

text.p: Pakistani President Farooq Leghari left for Uzbekistan on Friday with the Afghan conflict expected to dominate his talks with President Islam Karimov.

Leghari, who is due to visit Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan later this month, is expected to reassure his Central Asian hosts that the radical Islamic Taleban militia now ruling Kabul has no territorial ambitions beyond Afghanistan's borders.
The official news agency APP said Leghari, keen to expand Pakistan's ties with Central Asian states in energy, transport and communications, would sign several agreements in Tashkent.
Petroleum Minister Anwar Saifullah and officials from the communications and foreign ministries accompanied the president.
Leghari's tour coincides with plans to send a trade convoy overland to Central Asia, avoiding Afghanistan, which provides the most direct access routes to the former Soviet republics.

Twenty trucks carrying rice, wheat and leather goods are due to leave next week from the southern port city of Karachi to the Kazakh capital Almaty, symbolising Pakistani hopes of building trade ties with potentially oil-rich Central Asian nations.

The convoy's tortuous route -- trundling up the mountainous Karakoram Highway and across the Khunjerab Pass to the Chinese market town of Kashgar and on to the Kyrgyz capital Bishkek before winding up in Almaty -- reflects Pakistan's problems in finding ways to Central Asia that skirt its turbulent neighbour.
